title: Tomato Risotto
description: An oven-baked tomato and sausage risotto with fennel, basil and optional Parmesan at the table.
imageAlt: Reference photograph of a neatly plated tomato risotto on a white plate, topped with sun-dried tomatoes.
imageCaption: Reference photograph · sun-dried tomato variation · displayed crop
personalNote: Fennel and tomato are a lovely combination—the fennel lifts the tomatoes’ sweetness. Better a little less salty than too salty: we can always add salt, but we can’t remove it.
equipment: Large oven-safe pot with an oven-safe lid
advancePrep: Air-fry the sausages until fully cooked according to their packet, then cut into thin slices. Pick the basil leaves off their stalks.
importantNotes: Four portions means two dinners for both of us. If we eat a bit more on the first night, we can have garlic bread with the second dinner. Don’t wash this rice: we want the starch for creaminess. Use an oven-safe pot and lid. Keep Parmesan at the table if we want the second dinner dairy-free, and choose dairy-free sausage and stock too. For the batch, we can swap 300 g sausage for 500 g chicken or 500 g of 5% lean pork mince; check the swap note for the cooking changes. Times are estimates and don’t include air-frying the sausage.

ingredients.name: Vine-ripened tomatoes
ingredients.note: About 2 packs; slice. Or use 2 packs of salad tomatoes and the sugar below.

ingredients.name: Sausages
ingredients.note: Air-fry until fully cooked, then slice thinly. Choose dairy-free ones for the dairy-free second-dinner portions.

ingredients.name: Chicken stock cubes
ingredients.note: Check the ingredients if keeping second-dinner portions dairy-free.

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.note: Coarsely crushed, or use pepper powder.

ingredients.name: Basil leaves
ingredients.note: Pick the leaves off the stalks.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.note: Use only if substituting salad tomatoes for vine-ripened tomatoes.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.note: Only if needed after tasting; remember Parmesan adds saltiness too.

ingredients.name: Parmesan
ingredients.note: Add to individual servings if wanted. Leave out of the dairy-free second-dinner portions.

groups.title: If we want a little extra on night two

ingredients.name: Garlic bread
ingredients.note: Optional with the second dinner if we ate a bit more on the first night. Heat following the packet.

steps.title: Prepare and preheat
steps.description: Peel and chop the garlic and onion, then slice the tomatoes. Air-fry the sausages until cooked, following the packet, and slice them thinly. Put the oven on at 180°C and boil the measured water.

steps.title: Soften the onion and garlic
steps.description: Put the sliced sausage in the oven-safe pot on medium heat. Add the garlic and onion and fry for 5 minutes, until the onion softens.

steps.title: Cook the tomatoes down
steps.description: Add the tomatoes and chicken stock cubes. If we’re using salad tomatoes instead of vine-ripened ones, add the sugar too. Cook for 15 minutes, squishing it around, until the tomatoes go mushy.

steps.title: Add the rice and fennel
steps.description: Add the risotto rice WITHOUT washing it, and mix it through the tomato sauce. We want to keep its starch so the risotto goes creamy. Add the fennel seeds and mix again.
steps.tip: Fennel seeds look like cumin but are a little bigger and greener. Fennel and tomato are a classic combination: fennel lifts the tomatoes’ sweetness.

steps.title: Add the water and taste
steps.description: Pour in the boiled water and mix. Taste the liquid if the meat is fully cooked: we want it nicely salted, but a little less salty is fine because Parmesan adds saltiness later. We can always add salt, but we can’t take it out. Bring it to the boil.
steps.tip: Better a little under-salted than too salty: you can add salt later, but you can’t remove it.
steps.warning: If you swapped in raw chicken or mince, do not taste the liquid until that meat is fully cooked. You can check and adjust the seasoning after baking.

steps.title: Bake the covered risotto
steps.description: Once it starts boiling, put the oven-safe lid on and move the pot into the oven for 30 minutes. Use the oven gloves; those handles get hot.
steps.doneness: Cooked risotto rice. If using chicken or mince, check that the meat is fully cooked before serving.
steps.tip: For a chicken or mince swap, the centre of the meat should reach 75°C for 30 seconds. If it has not, continue cooking and check again before serving.
steps.warning: Use oven gloves. The pot, lid and handles will be hot, including after they return to the hob.

steps.title: Finish with pepper and basil
steps.description: Take the pot out carefully. Add the black pepper and basil leaves you picked off the stalks, and squish them through the risotto.
steps.doneness: Cooked risotto rice in a creamy tomato sauce.
steps.warning: Keep oven gloves nearby: the pot handles are still hot.

steps.title: Dinner tonight, and a little help for night two
steps.description: Add Parmesan to individual plates rather than the whole pot. This batch is for two dinners for both of us, so keep the second dinner aside. If we end up eating a bit more tonight, we can have what’s left with some garlic bread on night two—heat it following the packet.
steps.tip: Keep the cheese at the table instead of mixing it into the whole pot.

substitutions.title: Swap the protein
substitutions.text: For this original batch, interchange 300 g sausage with 500 g chicken or 500 g of 5% lean pork mince. The numbered ingredient quantities scale with the portion control, but these swap quantities describe the batch. Air-fry sausage until fully cooked according to its packet, then slice it. For chicken, cut into small pieces and cook it in the pot with the aromatics; it must be fully cooked by the end of baking. For pork mince, break it up in the pot and cook it through before continuing. If using raw chicken or mince, wait until the meat is fully cooked before tasting the cooking liquid.

substitutions.title: Salad tomatoes instead of vine-ripened
substitutions.text: For the batch, use 2 packs of salad tomatoes and add ½ teaspoon of sugar when cooking the tomatoes down.

substitutions.title: Black pepper
substitutions.text: Coarsely crushed pepper or pepper powder both work.

substitutions.title: Dairy-free second-dinner portions
substitutions.text: Leave Parmesan off the second-dinner portions, and choose sausages and stock cubes without dairy ingredients.

troubleshooting.title: Why leave the rice unwashed?
troubleshooting.text: Keeping its starch helps make the risotto creamy.

troubleshooting.title: A little less salty than expected?
troubleshooting.text: That is fine. Parmesan adds saltiness at the table, and you can add a little salt to a dairy-free portion if needed.

storage: Put the second dinner into small containers so it cools quickly, ideally within 1 hour. Keep it in the fridge and eat within 24 hours. Freeze it if we’re saving it longer, and keep Parmesan separate if we want it dairy-free.
reheating: Reheat once until steaming hot throughout. Stir or turn it during microwave reheating to avoid cold pockets.
foodSafety: Air-fry the sausages until fully cooked before slicing. Use an oven-safe pot and lid, and remember the handles stay hot after baking.
servingSuggestion: Two dinners for both of us. Add Parmesan to individual plates if we want it. If we eat a bit more on the first night, serve the second dinner with garlic bread.
